concept: Grammar-aware draft filtering for ngram and draft-model drafters
summary: speculative-decoding-with-structured-output-gram.md already holds verifier-side grammar handling and its asserted statement that no grammar-aware draft filtering exists; this file adds the drafter-side evidence for that statement.

facts.text: speculative-decoding-with-structured-output-gram.md already holds verifier-side grammar handling and its asserted statement that no grammar-aware draft filtering exists; this file adds the drafter-side evidence for that statement.

In `common/speculative.cpp` the draft-model drafter builds its per-sequence samplers with `top_k = 10` and `samplers = { TOP_K }` only, with no grammar field set, so the drafter proposes tokens without any grammar mask.

The draft sampler rebuild for rejection-style verification uses `samplers = { TOP_K, TEMPERATURE }` with top_k 10 at the target's temperature and a seed XORed with 0x85ebca6b, and again sets no grammar.

`common/speculative.cpp` registers five n-gram drafter types by name: ngram-simple, ngram-map-k, ngram-map-k4v, ngram-mod and ngram-cache; the file includes ngram-cache.h, ngram-map.h and ngram-mod.h.
A grep of the file for grammar or GBNF finds no match, so neither the n-gram drafters nor the draft-model drafter filter proposals against a grammar; filtering happens only at target verification.
